newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says 1997 budget to target growth.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says 1997 budget to target growth.

text.p: Nigeria's 1997 budget will switch emphasis from restoring economic stability to targeting growth and privatisating state-run companies, finance minister Anthony Ani said.

"We shall be talking of a budget of growth and development, a budget of reflation without inflation, a budget of selective but productive reflation," Ani said in a speech to the Lagos chamber of commerce on Wednesday night.

Tight fiscal policy imposed by military ruler General Sani Abacha over the past two years is credited with having reduced inflation and restored a measure of economic stability to sub-Saharan Africa's largest economy.
Ani predicted year-end annual inflation of between 27 and 30 percent, compared with over 70 percent last year.
He said the private sector would be expected to play a big role in plans for growth in 1997 and reemphasised the government's commitment to the privatisation of inefficient state-run companies.
"If government must provide the necessary amenities, government must allow the private sector to do what it is best suited and keep hands off private sector business," Ani said.
He said that in 1996 the government had been forced to dip into funds intended for other projects to support telecoms, power and railway companies.
"Government in embarking on its privatisation programme in 1997 will ensure honesty, transparency and accountability," he said.
Nigeria's annual budget is scheduled to be presented on January 1, but in recent years it has been delayed and the 1996 budget was not announced until February.
